This application has been filed by the applicants with the prayer to quash the summoning order dated 24.06.2019 passed by learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kaushambi as well as entire proceeding of Complaint Case No. 963 of 2018 (Reeta Rao Vs. sentences.text: Earlier an application u/s 482 No. 41102 of 2019 was filed by Uday Bhan and five others which is pending as against applicant no. 4 to 6 therein whereas with respect to applicant nos. 1 to 3, the aforesaid petition was dismissed.

Learned counsel for the opposite party submits that the opposite party has moved an application before the concerned court stating therein that she does not want to proceed against all the accused named in the first information report i.e. against all six persons.
Hence the present petition was filed by applicant Uday Bhan bearing no. 33201 of 2022 under changed circumstances as compromise has taken place between the parties.
On 19.11.2022, the following order was passed:-

"This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants for quashing the summoning order dated 24.6.2019 passed by learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kaushambi as well as entire proceeding of Complaint Case No.
963 of 2018 (Reeta Rao vs. Udai Bhan and others), under Sections 498A, 323, 504 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S. Mahewaghat, District Kaushambi.

963 of 2018 (Reeta Rao vs. Udai Bhan and others)

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for applicants and learned AGA for the State.
Sri Shivam Pandey, Advocate appeared on behalf of opposite party no.2.
He may file his vakalatnama in the Registry within a week.
Counsel for the applicants as well counsel for opposite party no.2 submit that the parties have entered into compromise.
A copy of compromise dated 25.8.2022 is annexed as Annexure -7 to the affidavit.

Accordingly, it is provided that the parties shall appear before the Court concerned along with a copy of this order within two weeks from today and be permitted to file an application for verification of the original compromise document.

It is expected that the trial court may fix a short date for verification of the compromise entered into between the parties and pass an appropriate order with respect to the verification within a period of three weeks thereafter.

Upon due verification, the Court below may pass appropriate order in that regard and send a report to this Udai Bhan And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177851122/
2 Court on or before 31.1.2023.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
List and connect this case along with the record of Application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. No.
41102 of 2019 in the additional cause list on 31.1.2023 before the appropriate Court.
Till the next date of listing no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants in the aforesaid case. "
In compliance of the aforesaid order, the report regarding verification of compromise received from ACJM, Kaushambi been placed on record as is evident from the office report dated 31.01.2023.

A letter dated 08.12.2022 of ACJM, Kaushambi has been placed on record along with affidavit as well as order dated 08.12.2022 by which the compromise has been verified in the presence of parties and their respective counsels.

Learned counsel for the applicants submits that since the compromise entered between the parties has been verified by the court below, the entire proceedings of the aforesaid criminal case may be quashed by this Court.

Learned A.G.A. for the State as well as learned counsel for the opposite party also accept that the parties have entered into a compromise and he has no objection, if the proceedings in the aforesaid case are quashed.
This Court is not unmindful of the following judgements of the Apex Court:
1. B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and Another; (2003)4 SCC 675,
2. Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation; (2008) 9 SCC 677,
3. Manoj Sharma Vs. State and Others; (2008) 16 SCC 1,
4. Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab; (2012); 10 SCC 303,
5. Narindra Singh and others Vs. State of Punjab; ( 2014) 6 SCC 466,
